METHOD & CONTEXT: Separation of what the source says, what the telemetry proves, and what requires new experiments.

column2: Is the sustainability agent worth its additional cost and complexity relative to the cost-only controller?
A cost-optimizing agent and a dual agent have been piloted on PV + BESS + building + grid telemetry.
Edge gateway, IoT platform and orchestration layer; telemetry connects OT assets with cloud agents.
The BDD case describes an industrial site; the supplied DATA_MODEL.pdf explicitly says residential building.
The operating traces have different PV soiling and different initial BESS SOC: not a controlled A/B experiment.
2026-01-05 11:00 to 2026-01-12 10:45, 15-minute timestamps, includes weekend and partial days.
Power kW, interval energy kWh, prices EUR/kWh, battery SOC fractional.
Net energy expense = SUM(grid import kWh x buy tariff - grid export kWh x sell tariff).
grid.cost is described as cumulative but is numerically equal to grid.power x applicable price / 60 at each sample.
No grid carbon intensity signal; report no verified CO2 impact, only defined proxies or scenario assumptions.
Exported energy can be battery discharge rather than only surplus PV; true PV self-consumption is unidentifiable.
Device chargeEfficiency and dischargeEfficiency are known (95% each). Ratios of weekly charge/discharge are NOT standalone round-trip efficiency.
Recover B 2026-01-09 20:00 energy flows via next cumulative - previous cumulative - next interval.
Building load kWh is estimated as instantaneous load kW x 0.25; B missing interval load not recovered.
Power balance is exact in recorded snapshots; interval energy integration differs within samples, so do not confuse them.
Telemetry does not include negotiation/decision logs; stated motives are not directly observable.
No observed violations or outages in the sample, so stress testing is needed to compare resilience.
